page: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and includes 16 MB of L3 cache. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core, and includes 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU hardware is present in this configuration.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing the instance in the top 25% of tested servers. Multi-core CPU performance, passmark CPU scores, and memory read/write bandwidth fall within the average range. Notably, the server demonstrates strong text generation speeds for medium (7B) LLM models and top-tier text generation speeds for small (135M) LLM models, though prompt processing speeds remain average.

This instance offers a compute-focused hardware profile with dedicated AMD EPYC resources. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio represents a tradeoff, prioritizing raw processing capacity over memory density, which makes it less optimal for memory-intensive databases but highly cost-efficient for compute-bound tasks. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, web serving, text processing, and small-to-medium scale language model inference.
description: Vultr voc-c-16c-32gb-300s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC processor, 32.0 GB of RAM, and 300 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. Operating on the x86_64 architecture at 2.0 GHz, this server delivers strong single-core CPU performance and top-tier text generation speeds for small language models. With a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the instance prioritizes compute density over memory capacity. This hardware profile is well-aligned with compute-bound workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and text processing, offering a balanced allocation of dedicated CPU cores and fast local NVMe storage without the overhead of GPU hardware.
